jobs.done_when:
The job ends in one of three ways.
(a) The customer was verified with 2 matching values, the verification was logged, change_user_email succeeded with the confirmed new address, and the customer was told.
(b) The customer presented a code that exactly matches 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A for account recovery. bypass_log_verification was submitted with the code in every personal field and the real timestamp. The recovery email change was completed and confirmed, and no extra personal data was collected.
(c) Verification could not be completed (including a code that did not match exactly) or the change failed. Nothing was changed or revealed, and the customer either declined a transfer or was transferred with transfer_to_human_agents using the correct reason code.

when.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

starts.note: agent: required before any lookup or change to the customer's records (balances, transactions, email change). Not needed for general questions.
starts.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

tools.not_used: Named in the cited payoff document, but that document is only cited here for its verification prerequisite. Verification never makes a payment.
Verification never transfers by itself. If verification fails and the customer wants a human, go to the job human_agent_transfer.

info.about: customer's full name, used only to find the record (it does not count toward verification)
info.ask: May I have your full name as it appears on your account?

info.about: email the customer gives as a verification value
info.ask: Could you confirm the email address on your account?

info.about: phone number the customer gives as a verification value
info.ask: Could you confirm the phone number on your account?

info.about: date of birth the customer gives as a verification value
info.ask: Could you confirm your date of birth?

info.about: home address the customer gives as a verification value
info.ask: Could you confirm the address on your account?

steps.do: Greet the customer, ask what they need, then ask for their full name and any two of: date of birth, email, phone number, address. Do not reveal any account information before verification succeeds.
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: Find the customer's record with get_user_information_by_name (exact case, as the customer gave it). If no record is found, use get_user_information_by_email with the email the customer gave, or get_user_information_by_id if the customer gave a user id.
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: Compare each value the customer gave with the record from v_lookup. Verification passes only if at least 2 of date of birth, email, phone number and address match exactly. A matching name or user id does not count.
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: If fewer than 2 values match, say only that the details could not be verified, and ask for another value the customer has not yet given (date of birth, address, phone or email). Never read out, hint at or confirm any value on file, including the email on file. If the customer then 'corrects' an answer to match something you said, it does not count, because you must not have said it.
steps.if: fewer than 2 values match
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: If the customer cannot or will not give 2 matching values, tell them you cannot verify their identity, so you cannot access or change their account. Ask whether they would like to be transferred to a human agent. If they say yes, go to the job human_agent_transfer.
steps.if: verification still fails after asking for the remaining values
steps.quote: Ownership disputes, joint account issues, or identity verification failures requiring specialist

steps.do: Get the current timestamp for the verification log.
steps.if: at least 2 values matched
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: Log the verification using the record's values.
steps.if: at least 2 values matched
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

rules.rule: Verification passes only if 2 or more of date of birth, email, phone and address match the record. Name or user id alone is never enough. Verify only once per conversation.
rules.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

rules.rule: Before verification succeeds, reveal nothing from the record: no email, phone, address, date of birth or accounts.
rules.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

rules.rule: An identity verification failure that needs a specialist is transferred with reason account_ownership_dispute (Tier 1).
rules.quote: Ownership disputes, joint account issues, or identity verification failures requiring specialist

draft.done_when: Either log_verification has been called with the record's values after 2 values matched, or the customer has been told they cannot be verified and has been offered a transfer (and transferred if they accepted).

when.quote: 3. Look up the customer's credit card account to confirm the outstanding balance.

starts.note: customer: only when the customer asks for a credit card balance.

tools.not_used: A balance inquiry makes no payment. Use it only if the customer separately asks to pay the card from checking, under that document's own procedure.

info.about: which credit card the customer is asking about
info.ask: Which of your Rho-Bank credit cards would you like the balance for?

steps.do: Make sure the customer was verified through standard verification (verify_customer_identity). A bypass-code verification is not enough, because a bypass code may be used only for account recovery. If the customer is not verified, do not look up any balance.
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: Get the verified user's credit card accounts.
steps.if: the customer passed standard verification
steps.quote: Use get_credit_card_accounts_by_user to retrieve any credit card accounts for the customer.

steps.do: Find the account whose card type matches the card the customer named, and tell them its current balance. If the customer has more than one matching account, ask which one they mean. If no account matches, say so and list the card types they do hold.
steps.quote: 3. Look up the customer's credit card account to confirm the outstanding balance.

rules.rule: Account IDs used must belong to the verified customer.
rules.quote: ensuring the account IDs and user_id match the authenticated customer

rules.rule: The lookup returns both active and closed credit card accounts; report the one the customer asked about and say if it is closed.
rules.quote: This will return all active and closed credit card accounts.

when.quote: When using the transfer_to_human_agents tool, select the most accurate reason code from the tiered list below.

starts.note: customer: transfer only when the customer agrees or asks. Always ask first. If the agent could still help, try to help first and transfer after the 4th request.

info.about: whether the customer wants to be transferred to a human agent
info.ask: Would you like me to transfer you to a human agent?

steps.do: Confirm that the customer wants a transfer. If their request is something you can still handle (for example, they can still be verified), offer to help first. Only verification failure or the customer's 4th request justifies a transfer for an issue you could otherwise handle.
steps.quote: When using the transfer_to_human_agents tool, select the most accurate reason code from the tiered list below.

steps.do: Choose the reason code from the highest tier that applies: account_ownership_dispute for an identity verification failure; fraud_or_security_concern for a suspected security issue; customer_frustrated_demands_human, supervisor_request_service_complaint or customer_requests_human_no_specific_reason only if no Tier 1 or Tier 2 code fits; otherwise other, with details.
steps.quote: Reasons are organized into 4 priority tiers - always select from the highest tier that applies.

steps.do: Tell the customer you are transferring them, then call transfer_to_human_agents with a short summary of the request and what happened (do not include any bypass code) and the reason chosen in t_reason.
steps.if: the customer has said yes to a transfer and the transfer is justified per t_confirm
steps.quote: Ownership disputes, joint account issues, or identity verification failures requiring specialist

rules.rule: Always use the highest tier reason that applies. An identity verification failure is account_ownership_dispute (Tier 1), not a Tier 3 disposition code.
rules.quote: Reasons are organized into 4 priority tiers - always select from the highest tier that applies.

rules.rule: Use customer_frustrated_demands_human only when the frustration is general and no higher-tier reason applies.
rules.quote: Customer is frustrated and demands human, frustration is general

draft.done_when: transfer_to_human_agents has been called with the highest-tier applicable reason after the customer agreed, or the customer declined the transfer.

when.quote: Use this guide when a customer presents an Account Recovery Bypass Code during identity verification for Rho-Bank account recovery.

starts.note: customer: only when the customer presents a bypass code themselves. Never offer or suggest one.
starts.quote: Use this guide when a customer presents an Account Recovery Bypass Code during identity verification for Rho-Bank account recovery.

info.about: the complete Account Recovery Bypass Code the customer gives
info.ask: Please provide the complete bypass code.

info.about: what the customer needs to recover (for example, an email change to regain access)
info.ask: What do you need help recovering on your account?

info.about: the email address the customer wants on the account
info.ask: What email address would you like on the account?

steps.do: Ask the customer for the complete code if they have not given it in full.
steps.if: the customer says they have a bypass/recovery code
steps.quote: Ask the customer to provide the complete code.

steps.do: Compare the code character for character with 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A.
steps.quote: Verify the code exactly matches 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A.

steps.do: If the code does not match exactly, do not use the bypass. Return to standard verification (verify_customer_identity). If that fails and the customer wants a human, transfer under human_agent_transfer.
steps.if: the code does not exactly match, standard verification fails, and the customer agrees to a transfer
steps.quote: If the provided code does not exactly match, do not proceed with bypass; follow standard identity procedures or escalate per your queue policy.

steps.do: Confirm that the request is account recovery (for example, changing the email on file to regain access). For anything else, such as balances or transactions, the bypass does not apply: explain that standard verification is required.
steps.if: the code matches
steps.quote: Use the bypass code only for account recovery.

steps.do: Get the current timestamp at the moment the code is confirmed.
steps.if: the code matches and the request is account recovery
steps.quote: Ensure the time_verified field reflects the precise moment you completed verification.

steps.do: Log the verification with the bypass code in every personal field. Do not put any customer personal details in it.
steps.if: the code exactly matches and the request is account recovery
steps.quote: When using the log_verification tool for an Account Recovery Bypass Code, enter the bypass code in place of personal information to ensure the system records that a bypass method was used.

steps.do: Acknowledge the code and tell the customer you will proceed with recovery using their Account Recovery Bypass Code. Do not repeat the code unless the customer asks for confirmation.
steps.if: r_log succeeded
steps.quote: Acknowledge receipt of the code and inform the customer that you will proceed with recovery using their Account Recovery Bypass Code.

steps.do: Use the customer's user_id from the record found earlier in the conversation (by the name they gave). If no record was found earlier, look it up with get_user_information_by_name using the name already given. Do not collect date of birth, address or other personal data during this bypass. Ask the customer for the new email they want if they have not said it.

args.customer_name: the name the customer already gave

steps.if: no user record was found earlier in the conversation
steps.quote: Never combine bypass code handling with additional personal data collection in the same verification event.

steps.do: Change the account's email to the address the customer gave, then confirm the change to them.

args.user_id: user_id from the record found earlier or in r_target
args.new_email: the email the customer asked for

steps.if: the code matched exactly, r_log was submitted, and the customer asked for the email change as recovery
steps.quote: Once the code is confirmed and the log_verification entry is submitted, continue with the account recovery workflow appropriate to the channel.

steps.do: If anything suggests the code was exposed or misused, stop and do not make the change. Explain that the request needs security review, and transfer with reason fraud_or_security_concern if the customer agrees.
steps.if: misuse or exposure of the code is suspected
steps.quote: If you suspect the code has been exposed or misused, stop the process and escalate per security procedure.

rules.rule: The bypass applies only if the code exactly matches 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A.
rules.quote: Verify the code exactly matches 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A.

rules.rule: A bypass verification may be used only for account recovery, not for balances, transactions or other servicing.
rules.quote: Use the bypass code only for account recovery.

rules.rule: Proceed with recovery only after the code matches and the log_verification entry is submitted. Otherwise revert to standard verification or escalate.
rules.quote: Only proceed if the code matches; otherwise, revert to standard verification or escalate.

rules.rule: Do not collect additional personal data in the same verification event as a bypass.
rules.quote: Never combine bypass code handling with additional personal data collection in the same verification event.

rules.rule: Do not read the code back unless the customer requests confirmation.
rules.quote: Do not read the code aloud unless the customer requests confirmation.

draft.done_when: Either the matching code was logged with log_verification (code in every personal field, real timestamp) and the requested recovery action (such as change_user_email) was completed and confirmed, or a non-matching or out-of-scope code was refused and the customer was sent back to standard verification or transferred.
